forecasts.question: Will a named senior Iranian official (FM Araghchi, SNSC spokesman, or Foreign Ministry spokesperson) issue a public statement explicitly calling for continued or renewed multilateral ceasefire negotiations — beyond restating Iran's seven conditions as preconditions — before EOD September 29, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Trump's September 25-26 rejection of Iran's UNGA ceasefire roadmap (Bloomberg, WSJ) creates an immediate decision point for Iranian diplomatic posture. FM Araghchi has been the consistent diplomatic face at UNGA and repeatedly framed ceasefire proposals as legitimate achievements; the IRGC's concurrent 'seven conditions, military ops continue' framing (Mohebbi Sep 26) creates an internal tension between the diplomatic and military tracks. The 72-hour window tests whether the diplomacy track survives the first formal US rejection — or whether Iran pivots to pure military posture.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-29, a named Iranian senior official (FM Araghchi, SNSC spokesman, or Foreign Ministry spokesperson) issues a public statement via IRNA, Tasnim, PressTV, or at an on-record press appearance affirmatively committing to or calling for continuation of multilateral mediated ceasefire negotiations — distinct from mere restatement of Iran's seven conditions as preconditions for any talks. A statement that the door remains open and Iran is prepared for a new round of mediator-hosted proximity talks counts. A statement that Iran will only talk if conditions are first met does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 source (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official by name; OR IRNA/Tasnim/PressTV official readout with named official confirmed by at least one TIER1 cross-reference.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Repetition of the seven conditions as preconditions without affirmative new-talks commitment = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. IRGC military statements without Foreign Ministry confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Unnamed 'Iranian official' = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Mediator asserting Iran 'open' without named Iranian official public statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: RESOLVE-YES if published before Sep 29

indicators.expected_effect: RESOLVE-YES if published before Sep 29

forecasts.question: Will a named senior US official (Secretary Rubio, Envoy Witkoff, Envoy Kushner, or White House NSC spokesperson) publicly respond — accepting, counter-proposing, or formally rejecting — Iran's September 23 ceasefire roadmap before EOD 2026-10-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast (Devil's Advocate addition). Iran set a four-to-five day deadline from its September 23 roadmap delivery. Trump reportedly briefed aides on his expectation to resume bombing after midterms (WSJ Sep 25-26), but this constitutes a private communication not a named public official statement per resolution criteria. The US historically does not ignore formal written diplomatic proposals, even to reject them publicly. However, the Trump administration has also routinely acted without formal diplomatic acknowledgment of Iranian overtures. p=0.50 reflects genuine uncertainty between a public rejection/counter-proposal and a deliberate non-response as implicit rejection.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-10-01, Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera reports a named US official's public statement that directly addresses, references, accepts, or formally rejects the written ceasefire roadmap handed to Witkoff/Kushner at UNGA on September 23; or if an official White House or State Dept press release specifically describes the US government's position on the document. NO if no such public named-official statement is published before EOD Oct 1.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing a named US official by title and name, explicitly referencing the September 23 Iranian document; OR official White House or State Dept press release carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: General statements about 'pursuing all diplomatic options' or 'remaining open to talks' without explicitly referencing the Sep 23 document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump social media posts alone, without State Dept or NSC confirmation, = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Mediator (Qatar, Pakistan) characterizations of US position without a named US official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. WSJ/Bloomberg reporting Trump told aides privately constitutes AMBIGUOUS-NO, not YES.

indicators.expected_effect: RESOLVE-YES if named in a public statement explicitly addressing the document

indicators.expected_effect: RESOLVE-YES if public and explicit; AMBIGUOUS-NO if via unnamed aides only

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire roadmap on Sep 25-26 (Bloomberg, WSJ), eliminating the near-term diplomatic path to mine-deployment halt or Hormuz partial reopening. AIS-visible transits on Sep 23 stood at 11 vessels; 10-day rolling average approximately 17-18 per day, roughly 57% of the 30-vessel threshold with only 7 days remaining before Oct 3 deadline. CENTCOM announced Sep 19 that US-escorted traffic cumulatively reached 1 billion barrels over two months, but day-count data confirms ongoing shortfall relative to the threshold. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi stated Sep 26 that military operations will continue until Iran's seven conditions are met. No P&I war-risk cover reinstatement observed; no Iranian halt-to-mine-operations commitment.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any AIS-based ship-tracking source (IMF PortWatch, Straits.live, MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: AIS-based tracker + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit; if trackers diverge by >20%, flag AMBIGUOUS.

forecasts.question: Will CENTCOM announce or carry out renewed kinetic strikes on Iranian territory onshore or Iranian coastal/port assets inside Iran's internationally recognized boundaries before EOD October 10, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. WSJ reported Sep 25-26 that Trump dismissed Iran's roadmap and briefed aides on expectation to resume bombing after November 5 midterm elections — explicitly framing the post-midterm timing as deliberate. The prior 17-day lull in confirmed onshore US strikes (longest since the Sep 1 re-escalation) coincided with UNGA week. The pre-midterm caution constraint reduces near-term escalation probability, but Trump also told aides his views 'could change,' and an Iranian provocation (mine deployment, tanker attack, US casualties) could trigger an immediate response regardless of midterm timing.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if CENTCOM official press release, DoD statement, or two independent TIER1 sources confirm US-launched kinetic strikes targeting Iranian-controlled territory, port infrastructure, or coastal assets inside Iran's internationally recognized land or territorial sea boundaries before EOD Oct 10, 2026. Strikes on Iranian proxy forces outside Iran, maritime interdiction in international waters, and strikes on Iranian-linked forces in Iraq/Syria/Yemen do NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM official statement; OR two independent TIER1 sources (Reuters, AP, WSJ, Bloomberg, NYT, BBC).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Strikes on Iranian-linked forces in Yemen/Iraq/Syria = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Maritime interdiction in international waters = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Unnamed official leaks without confirmed CENTCOM acknowledgment = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Weight toward NO; explicitly frames post-midterm timing preference per WSJ

indicators.name: CENTCOM announces strike on Iranian coastal, port, or interior infrastructure
indicators.expected_effect: RESOLVE-YES

indicators.name: Iranian provocation triggering immediate US kinetic response (mine deployment, tanker attack, US casualties)

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Four of five polls published September 17-24 placed Yashar at or ahead of Likud for largest-party status. Channel 12 (Sep 23): Yashar 23 seats, Likud 20. Channel 13 (Sep 24): Likud 18 seats, Eisenkot bloc leads 52-51 overall. Haaretz Sep 17: Netanyahu bloc marginally ahead but Likud individually well below 23. Single outlier — i24NEWS — gave Likud 27 seats and Yashar 22. Netanyahu's UNGA appearance and anti-ceasefire lobbying ran through this polling window; no single survey shows either bloc at 61 seats. Yashar at 22-23 in consensus polls and Likud at 18-20 leaves the plurality question open, but the directional trend runs against Likud plurality. Prediction markets (Polymarket) show Yashar at 62% vs Likud 39% for most-seats outcome.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

forecasts.question: Will a new Israeli governing coalition be formally sworn in and presented to the Knesset within 42 days of the October 27, 2026 election (before EOD December 8, 2026)?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Election is 31 days away; both major blocs currently polling well below 61 seats in most surveys (Netanyahu bloc: 50-51 seats; Eisenkot bloc: 51-52 seats). Israeli coalition formation historically requires 6-12 weeks minimum even in favorable fragmentation conditions. Arab party inclusion is resisted by both blocs but may be mathematically necessary for either to reach 61. The 42-day window is ambitious relative to recent Israeli formation timelines — the 2022-2023 government took 54 days; 2019-2020 attempts failed repeatedly. The wartime context could accelerate formation if a decisive security mandate emerges, or complicate it if war-management disagreements split potential partners.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Israeli President (or Acting President) formally notifies the Knesset that a new government has been sworn in, OR the designated formateur publicly announces a signed written coalition agreement covering 61 or more Knesset seats — both occurring on or before December 8, 2026. A caretaker government continuing in place does NOT count. A minority government sworn in with fewer than 61 signed coalition seats does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli President's Office official announcement; OR Knesset official record; OR two independent TIER1 sources (Haaretz, Jerusalem Post, AP, Reuters) confirming sworn-in status with coalition seat count confirmed at 61+.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition negotiations ongoing but no formal signing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Minority government (fewer than 61 seats) sworn in = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Agreement in principle without written signed document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Mandate granted but no sworn government by Dec 8 = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Either bloc wins decisive plurality >=28 seats enabling credible first-formateur path
indicators.expected_effect: Positive for rapid coalition formation; neither bloc at 28+ in current polls

indicators.name: Both blocs polling below 61 seats throughout October (fragmentation confirmed)
indicators.expected_effect: Weight toward slow formation; current polls: both blocs at 50-52 seats

indicators.name: Netanyahu public concession of plurality or mandate to Eisenkot facilitates rapid formation
indicators.expected_effect: Speeds formation by 10-15 days if Eisenkot wins plurality clearly

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVE-NO. Netanyahu's coalition completed the first full Israeli governmental term in four decades; the Knesset dissolved July 17 at its natural legal end, not by early vote or majority loss. The coalition served the full term with 61 seats intact through dissolution. Resolution criteria states: 'NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.' Both criteria triggers — (a) Knesset roll-call confirming majority loss and (b) Netanyahu announcing early dissolution with election before Oct 27 — failed to materialize. No residual pathway exists; caretaker government runs to Oct 27 election.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVE-NO. No TIER1 source, IRNA, Tasnim, or PressTV readout found any named Iranian official issuing a public statement committing to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations before EOD September 6. The Sep 1-6 window was defined by active kinetic exchange: US CENTCOM struck IRGC targets Sep 1, Iran launched ballistic missiles at US sites Sep 1, Kuwait air defenses engaged Iranian missiles Sep 2. Iran's declaratory posture in that window was confrontational. FM Araghchi actively rejected ceasefire framing as recently as August 19 (Middle East Monitor: 'Iran rejects ceasefire and demands a complete end to the war'). The next formally documented diplomatic contact occurred at UNGA on September 22-23 — 16 days after deadline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated, senior officials, named principals) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?

No TIER1 source, Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Swiss mediator readout, or second independent confirmation found of a formally convened Iran-US indirect negotiating session between Sep 3-17. The Islamabad MoU collapsed in July 2026; after the Sep 1 kinetic exchange, diplomatic activity was frozen. The first new formally mediated proximity session appeared at UNGA margins on September 22-23 — five days after deadline — when Qatari, Pakistani, and Egyptian intermediaries shuttled between Araghchi and Witkoff/Kushner delegations in New York (Al Jazeera Sep 23). Mediator 'in contact' activity in early September fell below the 'formally convened session' threshold per the ambiguity rule. Note: the Sep 22-23 UNGA session would have satisfied F3's substantive criteria had it occurred within the resolution window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session (not mere message relay) between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
